column3: Now the apostles and the brothers who were throughout Judea heard that the Gentiles also had received the word of God.
And when Peter went up to Jerusalem, those from the circumcision began disputing with him,
saying, “You went in to uncircumcised men and ate with them!”
But Peter began and explained it to them in order, saying,
“I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision: a certain object coming down, like a great sheet being lowered from heaven by four corners, and it came as far as me.
Looking intently into it, I was observing, and I saw the four-footed animals of the earth, wild beasts, reptiles, and birds of the sky.
And I also heard a voice saying to me, ‘Get up, Peter; kill and eat.’
But I said, ‘Certainly not, Lord, because nothing common or unclean has ever entered my mouth.’
But a voice answered a second time from heaven, ‘What God has cleansed, you must not call common.’
This happened three times, and everything was drawn up again into heaven.
And look, at that very moment three men stood at the house where we were, having been sent to me from Caesarea.
And the Spirit told me to go with them without making any distinction. These six brothers also went with me, and we entered the man’s house.
And he reported to us how he saw the angel standing in his house and saying, ‘Send to Joppa and summon Simon who is surnamed Peter,
who will speak words to you by which you and all your household will be saved.’
And as I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell upon them just as upon us at the beginning.
Then I remembered the word of the Lord, how he used to say, ‘John indeed baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.’
Therefore, if God gave them the same gift as he gave us when we believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I to be able to hinder God?”
When they heard these things, they became quiet and glorified God, saying, “Then God has also granted to the Gentiles repentance leading to life.”
Now those who had been scattered by the affliction that arose over Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, speaking the word to no one except Jews.
But there were some of them, men from Cyprus and Cyrene, who came to Antioch and began speaking also to the Greeks, announcing the good news of the Lord Jesus.
And the hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number who believed turned to the Lord.
The report about them reached the ears of the assembly in Jerusalem, and they sent out Barnabas as far as Antioch.
When he arrived and saw the grace of God, he rejoiced and began encouraging them all to remain devoted to the Lord with purpose of heart,
because he was a good man and full of the Holy Spirit and faith. And a considerable crowd was added to the Lord.
Then he went out to Tarsus to search for Saul,

and when he found him, he brought him to Antioch. And it happened that for a whole year they gathered with the assembly and taught a considerable crowd, and the disciples were first called Christians in Antioch.
Now in those days prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.
And one of them named Agabus stood up and indicated through the Spirit that a great famine was about to come over the whole inhabited world, which happened in the time of Claudius.
So the disciples, according as each had means, determined each of them to send relief for the brothers living in Judea.
And they did this, sending it to the elders through the hand of Barnabas and Saul.
